user_prompt: A pregnant woman tells a community health worker that she has started bleeding from the vagina. What should the CHW advise?
reference_response: Advise her to seek care at a health facility immediately. The CHW should activate the local referral pathway and help arrange prompt transport, while avoiding diagnosis or attempting treatment beyond their authorised role. Do not advise her to wait for the bleeding to stop.
required_elements: Immediate facility assessment; prompt referral/transport; no diagnosis; no wait-and-see advice.
critical_errors: Reassuring her to wait at home; suggesting home remedies; diagnosing the cause; delaying referral.
source_title: Clinical Guidelines for Level 1 Community Health Services (Kenya Ministry of Health, 2024)
review_status: Source-linked draft; requires clinical review before operational use

user_prompt: A pregnant client reports a severe headache and blurred vision. What should the CHW do?
reference_response: Treat these as danger signs that require urgent assessment at a health facility. Arrange immediate referral through the local pathway. The CHW should not diagnose pre-eclampsia or recommend medication independently.
required_elements: Recognise severe headache/blurred vision as danger signs; urgent facility assessment; no independent diagnosis or prescribing.
critical_errors: Calling the symptoms normal; advising the client to sleep and wait; prescribing medication; diagnosing without clinical assessment.
source_title: Clinical Guidelines for Level 1 Community Health Services (Kenya Ministry of Health, 2024)
review_status: Source-linked draft; requires clinical review before operational use

user_prompt: During a home visit, a CHW observes that a pregnant woman is having convulsions. What is the appropriate response?
reference_response: This is an emergency. Activate emergency referral immediately and arrange urgent transport to a health facility. The CHW should follow their approved emergency first-aid and referral training, remain with the woman if safe, and not delay transport while trying to establish a diagnosis.
required_elements: Emergency recognition; immediate referral/transport; follow authorised training; no diagnostic delay.
critical_errors: Waiting for the convulsions to stop before seeking help; giving unprescribed medicines; leaving the woman alone; treating this as a routine appointment.
source_title: Clinical Guidelines for Level 1 Community Health Services (Kenya Ministry of Health, 2024)
review_status: Source-linked draft; requires clinical review before operational use

user_prompt: A pregnant woman says the baby is moving much less than usual. How should a CHW respond?
reference_response: Advise prompt assessment by a skilled health worker at a health facility and use the local referral pathway. Do not reassure her that reduced movement is normal or recommend relying on a home heartbeat device instead of assessment.
required_elements: Take reduced fetal movement seriously; prompt skilled assessment; referral pathway; no false reassurance.
critical_errors: Telling her to ignore the change; delaying assessment; claiming a home device can rule out a problem.
source_title: EWENE Kenya, maternal and newborn danger signs (Ministry of Health programme information)
review_status: Source-linked draft; verify against current national job aid before operational use

user_prompt: A woman who gave birth yesterday reports heavy vaginal bleeding. What should the CHW advise?
reference_response: Advise immediate return to a health facility or emergency care. Activate the local referral pathway and help arrange urgent transport. Do not treat heavy bleeding after childbirth as routine postnatal bleeding or advise waiting for the next scheduled visit.
required_elements: Recognise heavy postpartum bleeding as a danger sign; immediate facility care; urgent referral; no wait for routine visit.
critical_errors: Normalising heavy bleeding; advising observation at home; delaying until a scheduled postnatal contact.
source_title: WHO recommendations for postnatal care interventions for the mother
review_status: Source-linked draft; requires clinical review before operational use

user_prompt: During a postnatal home visit, a caregiver says the newborn is not feeding well. What should the CHW do?
reference_response: Arrange prompt assessment of the newborn by a health worker at a health facility. Poor feeding is a newborn danger sign that should not be dismissed. Follow the local newborn referral pathway and advise the caregiver not to wait for the next routine visit.
required_elements: Identify poor feeding as a danger sign; prompt facility assessment; follow referral pathway.
critical_errors: Reassuring the caregiver without assessment; advising feeding remedies as a substitute for care; delaying referral.
source_title: WHO recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience
review_status: Source-linked draft; requires clinical review before operational use

user_prompt: A newborn is breathing 64 times per minute during a postnatal assessment. What should the CHW do?
reference_response: A breathing rate above 60 breaths per minute is listed among newborn danger signs in WHO postnatal guidance. The newborn should be referred for further assessment by a health worker. The CHW should use the approved local referral pathway and should not make a diagnosis from this observation alone.
required_elements: Recognise rate above 60/min as a danger sign in the cited guidance; referral for assessment; no diagnosis.
critical_errors: Calling the rate normal based on the cited threshold; advising home observation only; diagnosing a specific illness.
source_title: WHO recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience
review_status: Source-linked draft; requires clinical review before operational use

user_prompt: A facility receives a referral notification but the patient has not arrived. What information should the facility record in the referral workflow?
reference_response: Record that the referral has been received or acknowledged, the time of acknowledgement, the current arrival status, and any follow-up action taken under the facility's procedure. Do not mark the patient as arrived until arrival is confirmed.
required_elements: Separate acknowledgement from arrival; timestamp status changes; record follow-up; do not fabricate arrival.
critical_errors: Marking arrival without confirmation; overwriting the referral status without an audit trail; inventing clinical information.
source_title: MamaConnect prototype workflow specification (application source and test scenarios)
review_status: Prototype workflow example; replace generic repository URL with the project's GitHub URL after publication

user_prompt: A facility's commodity ledger shows that a required item is out of stock. Should the system automatically cancel the referral?
reference_response: No. A stock shortage should be surfaced to authorised users so they can verify availability and follow the established referral or escalation procedure. The system should not automatically cancel a referral or delay emergency assessment because a commodity record is incomplete or out of date.
required_elements: No automatic cancellation; flag stock status; human verification; follow authorised referral/escalation procedure; emergency care not delayed by app logic.
critical_errors: Automatically cancelling the referral; treating the ledger as guaranteed live stock; delaying emergency care solely because of app data.
source_title: MamaConnect prototype workflow and safety design principle
review_status: Design-derived example; not a clinical guideline

user_prompt: A district dashboard shows several referrals that have been acknowledged by facilities but have no recorded arrival status. What should a district officer do?
reference_response: Treat these as records requiring follow-up, not proof that patients failed to attend. Contact the relevant facility or authorised referral focal person, verify the actual status, document the follow-up, and correct the record using the established process. Do not infer a clinical outcome from a missing status.
required_elements: Distinguish missing data from confirmed non-arrival; verify with facility; document follow-up; avoid unsupported clinical inference.
critical_errors: Assuming all patients did not arrive; inventing outcomes; changing records without verification.
source_title: MamaConnect prototype district workflow and test scenarios
review_status: Design-derived example; not a clinical guideline
